'''Salar Kamangar''' ({{langx|fa|سالار کمانگر}}; born 1976<ref>{{Cite news |last=Seabrook |first=John |date=2012-01-08 |title=Streaming Dreams |url=https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2012/01/16/streaming-dreams |access-date=2026-01-25 |work=[[The New Yorker]] |language=en-US |issn=0028-792X}}</ref>) is an Iranian-born American senior executive at Google and former CEO of Google's YouTube brand.

==Early childhood and education==
Salar Kamangar, born in [[Tehran]],<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.delgarm.com/archer-lord.a317869 | title=زندگینامه نخبه های ایرانی/ سالار کمانگر مدیر عامل گوگل و یوتیوب کیست ؟ | date=30 June 2024 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://playback.fm/person/salar-kamangar | title=Salar Kamangar - Spouse, Children, Birthday & More }}</ref> holds a [[bachelor's degree]] in Biological Sciences with honors from [[Stanford University]] and was the 9th employee to join Google.<ref name="tmn">{{cite news|date=3 March 2011|title=Salar Kamangar, YouTube CEO, talks about the video site's future|work=The Mercury News|publisher=Digital First Media|url=http://www.mercurynews.com/2011/03/03/salar-kamangar-youtube-ceo-talks-about-the-video-sites-future/|access-date=4 September 2017|ref=tmn}}</ref> He joined after graduating from Stanford in 1998.<ref name="tmn" /> Kamangar attended Merced High School in Merced, California and graduated in 1994. He was voted "Most Likely to Succeed" by his graduating class. 

==Google==
On October 29, 2010, it was announced that Salar "SK" Kamangar, who was in charge of day-to-day activities, would replace [[Chad Hurley]] as [[CEO]] of [[YouTube]].<ref name="tmn" /><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.myfoxdfw.com/dpps/news/youtube-co-founder-steps-down-as-ceo-dpgapx-20101029-gc_10366544 |title=YouTube Co-Founder Steps Down as CEO |publisher=Myfoxdfw.com |date=2010-10-29 |access-date=2011-01-20 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101113070144/http://www.myfoxdfw.com/dpps/news/youtube-co-founder-steps-down-as-ceo-dpgapx-20101029-gc_10366544 |archive-date=2010-11-13 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.parsacf.org/Page/74 |title=Salar Kamangar Parsa Community Foundation |publisher=Parsacf.org |access-date=2011-01-20 |archive-date=2011-03-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110309153607/http://www.parsacf.org/Page/74 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was replaced as CEO of YouTube on February 5, 2014. His successor at [[YouTube]] was [[Susan Wojcicki]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://in.reuters.com/article/us-google-youtube-idINBREA141Y420140205 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305101920/http://in.reuters.com/article/us-google-youtube-idINBREA141Y420140205 |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 5, 2016 |publisher=Reuters |access-date=2013-02-05|title=Reuters }}</ref>

Before that, Kamangar created the company's first [[business plan]] and was responsible for its legal and finance functions.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2006-09-17/no-dot-13-google-the-search-ended-here |title=No. 13 Google: The Search Ended Here |date=September 18, 2006 |work=[[Bloomberg Businessweek]] |last=DeBruicker |first=John}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Levy |first=Steven |author-link=Steven Levy |year=2011 |title=In the Plex: How Google Thinks, Works, and Shapes Our Lives |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=V1u1f8sv3k8C |publisher=Simon and Schuster |isbn=978-1-41659-671-4}}</ref> From there, he became a founding member of Google's product team,{{citation needed|date=December 2012}} where he worked on consumer projects including the acquisition of [[DejaNews]] and the subsequent launch of [[Google Groups]].
